title: The bootstrap re-fetches the site manifest the wizard already holds, and three keys come ONLY from that second fetch
what: Both bootstraps fetch /api/v1/site unconditionally even when launched by the wizard; rclone_remote, sftp_shell_type and sftp_hostkey have no flag and come only from that second fetch. install-onboard-2 closed this class for canonical_prefix/tree_name only.
cost: Per install: one extra round trip (up to 8 s). When the second fetch fails, config.toml gets the site's remote name (ensure_config, cached manifest) while rclone.conf gets [ccsync_sftp]: every lane A/B pass fails on a green install, and the stanza is written without known_hosts_file, so the lanes trust any NAS host key until a re-run.
evidence: Windows param block has no RcloneRemote/SftpShellType/SftpHostKey; run_bootstrap passes neither; the fetch at :872 is unconditional.
fix: Pass the wizard's manifest to the child (e.g. CCSYNC_SITE_JSON env) and have both scripts use it in place of their own fetch when present; hand-runs keep fetching.

title: Windows and macOS bootstraps implement the same steps twice and have drifted; move the drifted steps into the companion CLI
what: Drift: (1) companion currency check size+mtime on Windows vs sha256 on macOS; (2) macOS boots out the running companion before replacing it, Windows copies over the live exe; (3) Syncthing REST wait 20x(3 s timeout + 1 s) on Windows (message says 20 s) vs 10x1 s plus a fixed sleep 2 on macOS; (4) temp staging cleaned on macOS, not on Windows; (5) macOS loads the companion agent before repairing rclone_path while Windows seeds config before launch (lanes bake rclone_path at construction, so a fast-reading companion runs with a bare name launchd cannot resolve - plausible race); (6) Windows confirms the launched PID after 3 s, macOS does not; (7) pinned versions and sha256s duplicated with no parity test. Both config-seeding blocks are dead in the wizard flow (ensure_config writes first).
cost: Every installer fix lands twice (MAC-9, INST-7, GL-28, CR-372 precedents) and the list above is what slipped. Estimated ~750 lines out of the .ps1 and ~650 out of the .sh if manifest resolution, pinned download + verify (parallel in Python), rclone stanza, Syncthing seeding, config seed/repair and device-ID parse move to companion subcommands, as --setup-resolve-prefs already did.
evidence: Line references in the .md finding; each drift read in both files.
fix: Parity fixes first (sha256 on Windows, one bounded wait, launch after config repair on macOS, a pin parity test); then companion subcommands both scripts call, keeping the scripts runnable standalone.

title: macOS install waits for Resolve to quit twice, back to back, each up to 180 s
what: run_resolve_mapping and run_resolve_prefs each call wait_for_resolve_quit with the full 180 s budget; when the first times out, the second almost always times out too.
cost: Once per Mac install with Resolve open: 3 extra minutes of dead wait. Today pgrep -x "DaVinci Resolve" may never match (bug-resolve-5), so the waits may not run at all; fixing that turns this on.
evidence: Two call sites with no shared timed-out state.
fix: Remember the first wait's verdict and skip the second wait when it already timed out; fix together with bug-resolve-5.

title: The Windows pinned download leaves ~130 MB of zips and extracted folders in %TEMP%
what: The downloaded zip and the extract dir under %TEMP% are never removed and the uninstaller does not know them; macOS uses mktemp -d with a cleanup trap. A re-run re-downloads even when a verified zip is present.
cost: Once per fresh install: rclone ~23 MB zip + ~65 MB extracted, Syncthing ~13 MB + ~30 MB, about 130 MB (estimated) left behind.
evidence: No Remove-Item of $zipPath/$extractDir after the copy.
fix: try/finally removing both after the copy, or a per-run stage dir; optionally reuse a zip that passes Test-PinnedDownload.

title: A hand re-run of windows_bootstrap.ps1 with -CompanionExeSource aborts at step 9 while the companion is running
what: Copy-Item over the running companion exe, outside any try, under ErrorActionPreference=Stop: a terminating error when the bundled exe differs. Autostart, Resolve prefs, launch, device ID and the capability summary never run. The wizard path is unaffected (clean slate kills the companion first).
cost: Each documented hand re-run on a live editor machine ends in a red error with an exit code other than 3, read as a hard failure.
evidence: macOS twin boots the agent out first (:2520-2522); windows_upgrade.ps1 kills, renames aside and retries for this reason.
fix: Stop the running companion only when a copy is needed, rename the live exe aside, copy, and catch/warn on failure, as windows_upgrade.ps1 does.

title: windows_upgrade.ps1 runs a full recursive ACL reset inside the companion-down window every upgrade
what: Between the kill (:184) and the relaunch (:530) the script re-grants ~/.ccsync and runs icacls /reset /T over every file under it, plus two secret-file icacls and a fixed 800 ms sleep; the companion's own state_acl.repair_if_needed already probes at start and repairs only on a denial.
cost: Per manual upgrade per machine: grant 0.27 s + reset 0.55 s per 5,000 files (measured on a synthetic tree) + ~0.2 s + 0.8 s sleep added to tray downtime; grows with ~/.ccsync.
evidence: Probe in scratch: grant 266 ms, /reset /T over 5,000 files 555 ms; state_acl.py:12-17.
fix: Move the ACL repair and secret-file tightening after the relaunch-and-confirm, or gate the recursive reset on the denied-file probe; replace the 800 ms sleep with Wait-Process on the killed PIDs.

title: build_editor_package's onboard.exe staleness check ignores four bundled inputs
what: $onboardInputs covers onboarding/*.py, windows_bootstrap.ps1 and the companion exe only; the spec also bundles drive_mapping.ps1, windows_uninstall.ps1, EULA.md and the licence files, so a change to any of them reports onboard.exe up to date.
cost: On runs without -RebuildOnboard (ship.cmd and CI always rebuild): new editors get the old uninstaller / drive-ownership guard while the loose package files are new, under a green report.
fix: Derive $onboardInputs from the spec's list, or glob installer\*.ps1 plus onboarding\assets and the licence files.

title: The base-rig wizard path never switches on Resolve's External scripting
what: CR-373's enable_resolve_scripting() (and --setup-resolve-prefs) run only in _worker_editor; the base finish page then always tells the user to set External scripting by hand.
cost: Every base-rig install: one manual Resolve preference, and a watcher/fixer/Cards agent that is silent until it is done.
fix: Call steps.enable_resolve_scripting() in _worker_base after the companion install; it already refuses safely while Resolve runs.

title: Locked exe copies renamed to .stale-<epoch> by the clean slate are never pruned
what: Each wizard run that meets a locked companion exe leaves a ~48 MB .stale-<ts> copy; COMPANION_FILE_NAMES and every later cleanup omit the pattern, so each re-run can add another.
cost: Rare per run, unbounded over re-runs: ~48 MB each, under the bin dir, the local root or the tree drive root (the uninstaller removes only the bin dir).
evidence: Repo-wide grep for 'stale-': steps.py:3360 and one test only.
fix: Add a *.stale-* glob over the same candidate dirs to build_cleanup_plan's exe list.
